 1. About the Initiative

The Digital Egypt Youth (DEY) initiative plays a vital role in achieving one of the strategic objectives of the ICT
 sector by empowering young Egyptians to thrive in the digital economy, contributing to the country’s
 socioeconomic development and digital transformation initiatives. 
 
 The Digital Egypt Youth (DEY) initiative aims to provide young Egyptians with the necessary skills and knowledge
 to thrive in the digital age. The initiative focuses on training youth in various digital fields to increase their
 employability and entrepreneurship opportunities. It specifically targets young Egyptians, equipping them with in-
 demand skills needed for jobs in the digital economy, and aims to bridge the digital skills gap in Egypt to create a
 digitally skilled workforce supporting the country’s digital transformation.
 The initiative offers a full-fledged scholarship and targets 2,500 fresh graduates from Egyptian universities
 nationwide. The initiative adopts an upskilling approach covering two aspects: technical upskilling and
 personal/soft-skills upskilling, seeking to cover various digital skills to cater to diverse interests and career paths.
 
 DEY collaborates with industry partners and experts to develop and deliver relevant training content, ensuring
 the program aligns with industry requirements and equips participants with practical, in-demand skills. The
 program facilitates job placement by partnering with industry stakeholders, creating linkages between trained
 individuals and potential employers through one month of on-the-job training at the industry partner’s premises.
 NTI has collaborated with more than 75 national and multinational industry partners — including Amazon (AWS),
 Etisalat Egypt, Vodafone, Huawei, WE, Cisco, VMware, Orange, Valeo, Avelabs, SEITech, Brightskies, and VOIS,
 among others — to design more than 30 professional tracks that meet job profiles and ICT market needs. At the
 end of the program, participants receive joint certification from NTI and the industry partners, validating their
 skills and competencies for future job opportunities. 
 
 A key target field of the Digital Egypt Youth initiative is Electronics & Embedded Systems, matching the
 presidential HireReady initiative. 
 Key facts: 
 
 Full-fledged scholarship for selected fresh Egyptian university graduates, within five calendar years of
 graduation. 
 Collaboration with 75+ national and multinational industry partners. 
 More than 30 professional tracks, each designed with industry partners to meet job profiles and ICT
 market needs. 
 Each track = 4 months total: Technical Program + Career Development (Soft Skills) Program, plus 1
 month of on-the-job training at an industry partner’s premises. 
 Candidates join after a fine screening process conducted in cooperation with industry partners.
 Successful candidates receive joint certificates from NTI and the industry partners.

 2. Common Program Structure 
 
 
 Every HireReady track follows the same two-part structure: 
 
 Part 1 – Technical Program: 294 hours, track-specific (details per track below).
 Part 2 – Career Development Program: 126 hours, identical across all tracks (detailed in Section 3).
 Total duration per track: 420 training hours (≈ 4 months), followed by 1 month of on-the-job training at
 an industry partner. 
 
 
 
 3. Career Development Program (126 Hours) — Common 
 to All Tracks 
 
 
 Overview 
 
 
 This comprehensive course is designed for aspiring professionals in the ICT field who aim to excel in international
 business environments. Participants develop proficiency in Business English, enabling them to confidently
 communicate and present in professional settings. Through hands-on simulations and workshops, attendees
 practice leadership and team-building skills, fostering autonomy and critical thinking.
 The course also covers essential soft skills, including effective communication, time management, and problem-
 solving, alongside a solid foundation in project management to manage projects efficiently across industries such
 as Construction and Information Technology. A focus on essential workplace skills prepares participants to thrive
 in a corporate environment, covering teamwork, conflict resolution, and professional ethics.
 
 3.1 Business English (35 hours) 
 
 Speaking about Careers: discussing career paths and professional experiences.
 Maintaining a Professional Online Image: building and sustaining a positive digital presence.
 CV Writing and interview preparation with the right language tools. 
 
 Telephoning and Arranging Appointments: phone etiquette and scheduling. 
 Email Writing for various business contexts. 
 Organizations and Corporations: corporate structures and functions. 
 Companies’ Structure and Activities: business models and operations. 
 Action Plan and Proposal Writing. 
 Business Meetings: conducting and participating effectively. 
 Writing Meeting Minutes.

 Soft Skills (42 hours) 
 
 Communication Skills (verbal and non-verbal). 
 Leadership Skills and Problem Solving. 
 Team Building. 
 
 Time Management. 
 Interviewing (job-interview preparation).

Presentation Skills. 
 Mentorship and Coaching. 
 Emotional Intelligence. 
 Stress Management. 
 
 Workplace Legal Considerations. 
 Managing Upwards. 
 Fit for Work (physical/mental well-being). 
 Motivation. 
 Workplace Ethics. 
 Change Management. 
 Corporate Social Responsibility. 
 Work-Life Balance. 
 
 Project Management (14 hours) 
 
 Project Management Framework. 
 Project Scope Management. 
 Project Schedule Management. 
 Project Cost Management. 
 Project Risk Management. 
 Project Monitoring and Controlling. 
 
 Advanced Tools (PM software and methodologies). 
 
 3.3 Essential Workplace Skills (35 hours) 
 
 Teamwork and Collaboration: building effective teams, role clarity and accountability, leveraging diverse
 skills. 
 Conflict Resolution: identifying/addressing conflicts, mediation skills, negotiation techniques.
 Professional Ethics: ethical decision-making, integrity and accountability, navigating ethical dilemmas.
 Adaptability and Flexibility: embracing change, resilience building, creative problem solving.
 Critical Thinking and Decision Making: analytical skills, problem-solving strategies, decision-making
 models. 
 Workplace Etiquette: professional communication, interpersonal skills, dress code and personal
 presentation. 
 Additional Skills for a Competitive Edge: networking skills, advanced time management, customer
 service excellence, innovation and creativity. 
 
 3.4 Capstone Project (Career Development track) 
 
 Participants prepare Capstone Projects throughout the course, integrating skills and knowledge from Business
 English, Career Development, Project Management, and Essential Workplace Skills. On the final day (6 hours),
 participants present their Capstone Projects, showcasing their ability to communicate, manage projects, and
 demonstrate acquired skills. 
 
 
 
 4. Category: Electronics and Embedded Systems 
 
 
 4.1 Digital IC Design — Code: E004 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours 
 Overview

Introduces students to digital electronics design and implementation on FPGAs (architecture, digital design flow,
 Verilog coding guidelines), with hands-on projects for basic digital blocks and complex FPGA implementations.
 Covers timing violations and power analysis using ISE & Vivado IDEs on Zynq-7000 development kits. Also covers
 ASIC design methodology (cost/size reduction through miniaturization and integration) and RTL-to-tape-out
 conversion, plus verification engineering: constructing a robust verification plan and complex UVM test cases for
 SoC designs. 
 
 Prerequisites 
 
 Good knowledge of digital electronics design. 
 Basic knowledge of HDL languages (VHDL/Verilog). 
 Basic knowledge of FPGA and ASIC technology. 
 Contents 
 
 Module 1: Digital Design with FPGA Digital systems design review; top-down digital design flow; introduction
 to FPGAs and FPGA architecture; FPGA flow overview; ultrafast design methodology; VHDL/Verilog motivation,
 modules, operators, combinational/sequential logic; simulators; hierarchical design; blocking vs non-blocking
 assignments; test-benches; functions/packaging/tasks; compiler directives; system tasks; finite state machines;
 design constraints; timing analysis; FPGA tool design flow; Project 1 (UART); scripting languages.
 
 Module 2: Digital Design ASIC ASIC introduction; STA basics and timing paths; FF requirements and timing
 constraints; EDA tool design objects; logic synthesis; formal verification; synthesis tutorial and project; floor
 planning, power planning, placement, ICC; CTS, routing, chip finishing; complete synthesis/formal
 verification/PNR/STA tutorial (2 parts); extraction and STA; EMIR and power estimation; final project.
 Module 3: Digital Design Verification Verification basics; System Verilog (data types, process blocks,
 hierarchical structures, compiler directives, scheduling, assignments, classes, randomization, coverage); UVM
 overview, hierarchy, base classes, factory, phasing, resources/configurations, TLM, sequences/sequencers,
 components, full environment, UVM testing lab; Design for Testability (DFT).
 
 Hands-On: Labs using FPGA kits (e.g., Zynq-7000); writing VHDL/Verilog and System Verilog programs.
 
 
 4.2 Electronics Design for Industry — Code: E006 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours 
 
 Overview 
 Prepares hardware designers capable of developing complete, production-ready electronic designs for smart
 devices (washing machines, water heaters, meters, access controls, cars, etc.). Targeted skills: design/simulation
 tools, sensors and actuators, linear and switched-mode power supplies, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), PCB
 tools, thermal design, and reliability/lifetime estimation. 
 
 Prerequisites 
 
 Basic knowledge of circuits. 
 Basic analytical skills. 
 Basic knowledge of statistics. 
 
 Contents 
 
 Basic Electronic Design (96 hr): Circuit simulation (LTSpice — transient, AC, DC, parametric, Monte Carlo);
 ADC types, performance, limitations; transducers and actuators; analog signal conditioning and filter design; op-
 amp circuits (amplifiers, active filters, level shifters, instrumentation, multi-vibrators, log, rectifiers) with practical
 limitations; oscillators; galvanic isolation; protection (ESD/HBM, transient protection, MOV/TVS selection); comm
 buses (RS232/422, I2C, SPI, UART, CAN); practical transistor circuits (BJT, MOS switches, relay drivers); heat sink
 sizing.

Power Supply Design (96 hr): Switching-mode power supply basics; passive/active component parasitics; non-
 isolated and isolated DC/DC converter design; inductor/transformer design; EMI filter design; efficiency analysis.
 
 PCB Design for Manufacturing & EMC (96 hr): PCB design tool, component management, layer stack and
 layout, library/reuse; Design for Manufacturing (DFM) — manufacturing processes, reliability/lifetime calculations;
 Design for EMC — concepts and standards, conducted/radiated emission and immunity (setup, mechanisms,
 mitigation), PCB EMC design guidelines (board structure, digital/analog/high-speed/high-voltage, shielding).
 Hands-On: Sensor interfacing/calibration labs; PCB design tool; 10W flyback power supply design lab; EMC labs
 (conducted emission evaluation); power supply lifetime estimation. 
 
 
 5. Category: Network Infrastructure and Enablers 
 
 
 5.1 Core Data Network Infrastructure — Code: N002 
 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours 
 Overview 
 
 Trainees learn core enterprise network knowledge through hands-on experiences, starting with core services on
 Linux & Windows servers, then CCNP ENCOR (dual-stack IPv4/IPv6, virtualization, infrastructure, network
 assurance, security, automation), then CCNP ENARSI (advanced routing, Layer 3 VPN, infrastructure
 security/services). Security is covered via FortiGate firewall labs (FortiOS Administrator).
 
 Targets Communication/Electronics Engineers, Computer & Information graduates, and job seekers for
 professional-level ICT roles. Leads to Red Hat RHCSA (EX200), Cisco 350-401 ENCOR, Cisco 300-410 ENARSI, and
 Fortinet NSE4 certifications. 
 Prerequisites 
 
 CCNA 
 
 Contents 
 
 Microsoft Windows Server administration; CCNP Enterprise – Core Networking (ENCOR); CCNP Enterprise –
 Advanced Routing (ENARSI); Linux Red Hat System Administration (RHCSA); Red Hat Ansible for Network
 Automation; FortiOS Administrator (Fortinet NSE4). 
 Hands-On: Simulation tools, emulation tools, local & remote real labs. 
 
 Job Profiles: NOC Engineer, Network Engineer, System Admin Engineer, IT Infrastructure Engineer, IT Specialist
 Engineer.

Linux Foundations 
 Cloud Foundations

 AWS Cloud Practitioner; AWS Solutions Architect; AWS Cloud Security; Docker & Containers & Kubernetes; Red
 Hat OpenShift Administration I (DO180); Huawei Cloud HCCDA-TE; Huawei Cloud HCCDP-Cloud Migration.

 5.3 Advanced VoIP and Collaboration Networks — Code: N004 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours 
 
 Overview 
 Covers unified communications networks — voice, video, and data sessions — using Cisco and Avaya equipment.
 Prepares candidates for: CCNP Collaboration Call Control and Mobility (CLACCM 300-815), CCNP/CCIE
 Collaboration Core (CLCOR 350-801), Avaya Aura Core Components Integration (71200X), Avaya IP Office
 Platform Basic Integration and Configuration (77200X). 
 
 Prerequisites 
 
 CCNA 
 
 Contents 
 
 Part I: Cisco-Based Solution AV Fundamentals (unified collaboration, SIP/H.323, RTP/RTCP/DTMF, Cisco
 converged collaboration); Endpoints (phones, Telepresence, registration, call settings, maintenance); Network
 Requirements (core network components, L2/L3 QoS, DNS/NTP/SNMP); Call Control Mechanisms (Unified CM
 routing/dial plans, LDAP integration, SIP registration, CAC, globalized call routing, SIP trunk config, call control
 features, mobility, CUBE routing/interworking, Unified CME/SRST); Edge Services (MRA, IOS XE gateway/media
 resources); Collaboration Applications (Unity Connection, IM & Presence, Jabber); Troubleshooting (endpoints,
 CUCM reports, RTMT, Disaster Recovery System, voicemail monitoring). 
 Part II: Avaya-Based Solution Avaya Aura overview and components; Communications Manager
 administration, telephones, dial plan, basic/enhanced features, COS/COR administration, group features, outgoing
 calls/trunks (ISDN-PRI, SIP, H.323, AAR/ARS), maintenance/security; Avaya Aura System Manager; Session
 Manager (SIP registration, routing policy, maintenance); Communication Manager integration (duplex config, TLS
 certificates); Avaya Aura Media Server; Avaya IP Office Platform Administration (manager modes, security,
 general/user settings, SIP trunks, short codes, button programming). 
 Hands-On: Exercises using Cisco Collaboration and Avaya Aura equipment. 
 
 
 5.4 Microsoft Azure Administration — Code: I007 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours 
 
 Overview 
 
 Eight-course series covering core Windows Server 2016/2022 infrastructure (AD DS, networking services, Hyper-
 V), Azure fundamentals, Azure Administrator skills (subscriptions, VMs, storage, virtual networking, backup,
 hybrid connectivity, Azure AD), Azure networking design (hybrid connectivity, routing, private access,
 monitoring), Azure security (identity/access, platform protection, data/apps, security operations), and Windows
 Server Hybrid Core Infrastructure administration.

Prerequisites 
 
 Communications and Electronics Engineering / Computer Engineering / Computer Science graduate.
 CCNA 
 
 Contents 
 
 Windows Server 2016/2022 Administration (137 hr): IPv4 network planning, DHCP, DNS, server
 deployment/images, local storage, domain controllers, AD DS object management, VM management, VPNs,
 enterprise storage, Storage Spaces/Data Deduplication, Hyper-V, advanced AD DS (sites, replication), high
 availability/DR, failover clustering, NLB, Group Policy, securing/monitoring/recovering AD DS.
 AZ-900 Azure Fundamentals (7 hr): cloud computing/service models, Azure architecture,
 compute/networking/storage services, identity/access/security, cost management, governance/compliance,
 resource management, monitoring. 
 
 AZ-104 Azure Administrator (36 hr): Azure AD, users/groups, subscriptions, Azure Policy, RBAC, ARM
 templates, virtual networks/NSGs/Firewall/DNS/peering/VPN Gateway/ExpressRoute/Virtual WAN, routing/Load
 Balancer/App Gateway, storage accounts/Blob/security/Files, VM configuration/availability/extensions, App
 Services/Container Instances/AKS, backups, Monitor/alerts/Log Analytics/Network Watcher.
 AZ-700 Networking Solutions (36 hr): virtual networks, hybrid networking, load balancing (HTTP/non-HTTP),
 network security, private access to Azure services, network monitoring. 
 
 AZ-500 Security Technologies (36 hr): Azure AD security, hybrid identity, AD identity protection, PIM,
 governance strategy, perimeter/network/host security, container security, Key Vault, application/storage/SQL
 security, Monitor, Defender for Cloud, Sentinel. 
 AZ-800 Hybrid Core Infrastructure (36 hr): AD DS, domain controllers/FSMO, GPOs, hybrid identity, Azure
 IaaS AD DCs, secure administration, JEA, hybrid workloads/Azure Arc, Hyper-V and containers, Kubernetes
 orchestration, IaaS VM planning/customization/automation, DHCP/DNS/IPAM/remote access, hybrid networking,
 file servers, Storage Spaces Direct, Data Deduplication, iSCSI, Storage Replica.
 
 Job note: Hands-on demonstrations throughout.

 6. Category: Cybersecurity 
 
 
 6.1 Defensive Security Solutions — Code: S008 
 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours 
 Objectives 
 
 Explores cyber-criminal tactics and the technologies/products/procedures cybersecurity professionals use to
 combat cybercrime. Covers core network security concepts and skills for maintaining confidentiality, integrity,
 and availability. Extensive hands-on labs on Cisco Firepower, Fortinet FortiGate, Sophos, and Palo Alto solutions.
 
 Prerequisites 
 
 Engineering (Communications/Electronics or Computer Engineering), Information & Computer, IT, or
 Computer Science graduates. 
 CCNA (certified or equivalent course). 
 Contents 
 
 Network and Security Fundamentals (49 hr): network design principles, IPv4/IPv6 review, router/switch
 config (VLANs, routing), cyber-criminal TTPs, firewall technologies, secure VPNs, IPS role,
 confidentiality/integrity/authentication. 
 
 Cisco Security Solution (49 hr): NGIPS/NGFW concepts; Cisco ASA (Firewall, NAT, AAA); Firepower Threat
 Defense setup; access control policies; security intelligence; site-to-site VPN; remote-access SSL VPN with
 AnyConnect; Firepower for IPS/threat management/web filtering. 
 Fortinet Security Solution (120 hr): - FortiGate Administration (42 hr): operation modes, GUI/CLI, Security
 Fabric, firewall policies, NAT, user authentication, encryption/certificates, SSL/TLS inspection, application control,
 anti-DoS, SSL VPN, IPsec VPN, logging. - FortiManager (21 hr): central management, provisioning templates,
 policy packages, Security Fabric integration, HA/backup/recovery, firmware management, troubleshooting. -
 FortiAnalyzer (21 hr): central logging, architecture, access controls, HA, log management, event/incident
 management, reporting. - FortiMail (28 hr): email security architecture, LDAP integration, SMTPS/TLS/IBE, anti-
 spam, anti-phishing, FortiSandbox ATP integration, DLP, dashboards. - FortiWeb (28 hr): WAF fundamentals,
 deployment, load balancing, ML capabilities, signatures, anti-DoS/defacement, SSL/TLS, authentication, PCI DSS
 compliance, caching/compression, content routing/rewriting. 
 
 Sophos Security Solution (28 hr): architecture, security/NAT policies, GUI/CLI administration, network
 protection, site-to-site VPN, authentication, web protection/application control, remote access VPN, wireless
 protection, logs/reports, Sophos Central management. 
 Palo Alto Security Solution (28 hr): NGFW security features, security/NAT policies, certificate operations, SSL
 VPN, IPsec VPN, threat prevention. 
 
 Hands-On: Simulation tools, virtual machines, remote cloud labs. 
 
 Job Profiles: Network Security Engineer, Cybersecurity Engineer, Security Solutions Specialist.
 
 6.2 Security Operation Center (SOC) Engineering — Code: S005 
 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours 
 Overview

Teaches penetration testing and ethical hacking principles and the tools/techniques hackers use. Trains forensic
 analysis to trace and report evidence using Security Onion, QRadar, FortiAnalyzer, FortiSIEM, and FortiSOAR, and
 teaches Incident Response Plan preparation. 
 
 Prerequisites 
 
 Engineering (Communications/Electronics or Computer Engineering), IT, or Computer Science graduates.
 CCNA (or equivalent). 
 Contents 
 
 Network Fundamentals (14 hr); Linux RedHat Administration-I (28 hr); FortiGate Operator (21 hr) —
 firewalls/NGFW, user authentication, SSL inspection, web filtering, IPS, application control, IPsec/SSL VPN;
 Network Penetration Testing (56 hr) — reconnaissance, scanning, vulnerability analysis, web app pentesting,
 social engineering, system exploitation, wireless pentesting; Cisco Cyber Security Associate (42 hr) — threat
 intelligence, forensic analysis, SOC operations, Security Onion, endpoint investigation, network intrusion analysis;
 FortiAnalyzer Analyst (21 hr); FortiSIEM (28 hr); FortiSOAR (21 hr); SPLUNK (28 hr) — searching, dashboards,
 correlation, reports/alerts, visualizations; IBM QRadar (35 hr) — architecture, data flows, log sources, CRE, Use
 Case Manager, asset management, AQL, reporting. 
 
 Hands-On: Simulation tools, virtual machines, remote cloud labs. 
 
 
 6.3 Red Team Penetration Tester — Code: S011 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours 
 Overview 
 
 Equips participants with the penetration testing lifecycle: planning, reconnaissance, scanning, and exploitation
 across web applications, networks, and mobile environments. Emphasizes documentation, legal/ethical
 standards, and real-world problem-solving. 
 
 Target Audience / Prerequisites 
 
 Communications and Electronics / Computer Engineering / Computer Science graduates.
 CCNA 
 
 Contents 
 IP Networking Review (21 hr); Linux Administration (35 hr) including Bash scripting; Python (21 hr) — data types,
 syntax, Jupyter, data structures, functions, classes; Firewalls and Cryptography Basics (28 hr); Web Application
 Fundamentals (35 hr) — HTML, CSS, client-side scripting, PHP, SQL; Web App Penetration Testing (70 hr) —
 authentication/access-control vulnerabilities, OS command injection, SQL injection, file upload vulnerabilities,
 SSRF, path traversal, XSS, CSRF, CORS; Network Penetration Testing (56 hr) — footprinting/reconnaissance,
 scanning, exploit/pivot, enumeration, system hacking, malware, sniffing, social engineering, DoS, evading
 IDS/firewalls/honeypots, wireless hacking, privilege escalation, Active Directory attacks, reporting; Mobile App
 Penetration Testing (28 hr) — Android pentesting. 
 
 Hands-On: Labs on virtual machines. 
 Job Profiles: Penetration Tester (Red Team), Vulnerability Analyst, Security Analyst, Ethical Hacker.

 Practitioner (CLF-C01), AWS Solutions Architect Associate (SAA-C03), AWS Security Specialty (SCS-C03).

 CCNA 
 
 Fundamentals of Linux and Cloud Concepts

 Solutions Architect; AWS Cloud Security Foundations; Red Hat Enterprise Linux Automation with Ansible (RH294);
 Kubernetes/Helm; Red Hat OpenShift Introduction to Containers; Red Hat OpenShift Development I (DO188); Red
 Hat OpenShift Administration I (DO180); Infrastructure-as-Code tools (Terraform/CloudFormation/Ansible); Git;

 7.2 Professional DevSecOps Engineer — Code: D004 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours 
 
 Overview 
 
 Embeds security throughout the software delivery lifecycle while retaining DevOps speed and agility:
 Linux/Bash/Python basics, Agile, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS fundamentals, Terraform, Ansible, OpenStack, and
 secure CI/CD. Prepares for DASA DevOps Fundamentals, Certified DevSecOps Professional, and AWS Solutions
 Architect Associate (SAA-C02) exams. 
 Target Audience / Prerequisites 
 
 Communications and Electronics / Computer Engineering / Computer Science graduates.
 CCNA 
 
 Contents 
 
 Linux Fundamentals and Bash Scripting (35 hr) — file/user/service management, remote access, hardening; Git (7
 hr); Python (22 hr) including secure coding (input validation, Paramiko, PyCrypto); Agile and DevSecOps
 Fundamentals (14 hr); Docker (21 hr) — secure Dockerfile creation, image scanning, secure networking, Docker
 Compose/Swarm, kaniko/DinD; Kubernetes (49 hr) — architecture, resource creation, networking/services, RBAC,
 network/pod security policies, Kubernetes security best practices, EKS, Istio service mesh/zero trust, HashiCorp
 Vault/AWS Secrets Manager integration; AWS Fundamentals (49 hr) — networking (VPC, subnets, routing, NAT,
 peering, Transit Gateway), core services (EC2/ECS/Fargate/EKS/Lambda/API Gateway/CloudFront/Route53),
 storage/databases, CloudFormation, monitoring, IAM security, Security Hub/GuardDuty; OpenStack Cloud
 Platform (21 hr); Terraform (21 hr) — IaC, state, modules, workspaces, Sentinel policies, HashiCorp Vault intro;
 Ansible (14 hr) — inventory, roles, hardening automation, Ansible Vault; Monitoring (7 hr) — Prometheus; CI/CD
 and DevSecOps Pipeline (28 hr) — Git, secure pipelines, Snyk/OWASP ZAP/Clair integration, GitLeaks, SonarQube,
 ArgoCD; practice project (secure end-to-end DevSecOps pipeline). 
 Job Profiles: DevOps/DevSecOps Engineer, AWS/OpenStack Cloud Administrator, Security-focused SRE, Cloud
 Security Specialist.

8. Category: Telecom Engineering 
 
 
 8.1 M-NOVA: Mobile Network Planning, Optimization, Virtualization and 
 
 Automation — Code: W003 
 
 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours (42 training days) 
 
 Overview 
 Transforms engineering graduates into enterprise-ready autonomous network engineers via academic rigor plus
 extensive hands-on lab work, automation, and business skills — aiming for a competence level equivalent to 2–3
 years of industry experience. Core focus: end-to-end RAN Planning and Optimization integrated with Automation
 and AI. 
 
 Prerequisites 
 
 Electronics and Communications Engineers. 
 Contents (by Phase) 
 
 Phase 1 – Deep Foundations & Legacy Networks (3G/4G LTE), Days 1–7: mobile network ecosystem, site
 components; 3G UMTS fundamentals and link budget; 4G LTE architecture (E-UTRAN/EPC); 4G RF planning (link
 budget, PCI planning); 4G optimization — accessibility/retainability, mobility management; Phase 1 milestone
 assessment (practical lab exam). 
 
 Phase 2 – 5G Standalone (SA) Architecture & Planning, Days 8–14: 5G SA core/RAN architecture (SBA,

 10. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) 
 
 
 1. Who is eligible to apply for the scholarship? Anyone who has not graduated more than five years ago.
 
 2. Does studying require attending the institute’s premises? Yes, the initiative is available through the
 attendance system at the institute’s locations. 
 3. Is there practical training or is the study purely theoretical? The study includes both theoretical and
 practical aspects; practical training is conducted based on the training-unit content using the latest methods and
 specialized programs.

4. Are employees allowed to join the scholarship? Full commitment to attending lectures daily throughout
 the training unit is required to be eligible. 
 
 5. What is the duration of the training unit? 3 months at the institute’s premises, plus 1 month of practical
 training at one of the companies supporting the selected training unit. 
 6. If I previously benefited from the institute’s scholarships (6-month or 3-month), can I apply for
 the new training units? You can only benefit from the “HireReady” and “Digital Egypt Youth” initiatives once.
 
 7. Do I need a computer to join the scholarship? Preferable to have a personal laptop; if not possible, NTI
 provides a computer throughout the training period at the premises. 
 
 8. When will I be contacted for the interview? Once the application period closes, you will be contacted to
 schedule acceptance tests, which require your presence at the premises on the specified date.
 9. When will I be notified of the interview results? Within two weeks after the interview. If accepted and
 the required number of participants is complete, you’ll be contacted to confirm paperwork and readiness to
 participate. 
 
 10. What should I do if I entered incorrect information in the registration form? Email D4m@nti.sci.eg
 with your full name and national ID number for follow-up. 
 11. How can I change my preferences? Email D4m@nti.sci.eg requesting deletion of all preferences, then
 enter new preferences using the same account. Modifications are treated as a new registration starting from the
 modification date. 
 
 12. When is an applicant considered accepted for the scholarship? Three stages: (1) meeting all training-
 unit requirements listed on the registration page; (2) completing the personal interview; (3) submitting all
 required documents. 
 13. How can I withdraw from the scholarship? Send a withdrawal request at least 48 hours before training
 starts, including full name, national ID number, training unit applied for, and registration number, to
 D4m@nti.sci.eg. 
 
 14. Can non-Egyptian nationals apply for the scholarship? The scholarship is only available for Egyptians.
 
 15. Details about the 4-month scholarship (attendance, duration, online/offline)? 5-day work week, 7
 working hours/day, morning sessions, attendance required at the institute’s premises throughout. NTI provides
 free transportation from anywhere in Cairo to the premises during the initiative.
 16. What is the deadline for submitting the certificate? Before the start of the acceptance-test phase.
 
 17. Will financial incentives be provided during training? Yes, a monthly allowance is provided throughout
 the 3-month training period at the premises. 
 18. Does the scholarship require a specific GPA? No specific GPA is required — only selecting an eligible
 specialty and passing the acceptance tests.

NTI–Huawei Egyptian Talents Academy (ETA) 
 
 National Telecommunication Institute (NTI) & Huawei Egypt 
 
 Source: https://www.nti.sci.eg/eta/ 
 
 
 
 About the Initiative 
 
 The Egyptian Talents Academy (ETA) is a partnership between the National Telecommunication Institute
 (NTI) and Huawei Egypt, under the auspices of Egypt's Ministry of Communications and Information
 Technology (MCIT). It aims to build the digital capabilities of Egyptian students and university graduates
 through Huawei's advanced technology training programs, supporting Egypt's Vision 2030 toward a digital
 society. 
 
 Training is delivered at NTI branches and Creativa Innovation Hubs spread across almost all Egyptian
 governorates, moving trainees from basic levels up to associate, professional, and expert levels (Huawei's
 HCIA fi HCIP fi HCIE certification path). ETA aims to train 15,000 Egyptian youth over five years across
 
 fields including data networks (Datacom), cybersecurity, 5G, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and
 big data. 
 Certification incentives: outstanding trainees can sit the official Huawei international certification exam
 for free; other trainees get a 70% discount on exam fees; and the top 10% of high-achieving graduates
 
 receive vouchers covering 100% of the international exam fees. 
 
 Key Facts 
 
 
 Organizers NTI + Huawei Egypt, under MCIT 
 
 Certification track Huawei ICT Academy levels: HCIA (Associate) fi HCIP (Professional) fi HCIE (Expert)
 Typical level-1 duration Minimum ~70 study hours (increases with training level); e.g. the AI track ran 80 hours / 12 technical lectures over 2 weeks, morning (9am–3pm) or evening (3pm–9pm) sessions
 
 Cost Free scholarship (MCIT-funded); certification exam discounts as above
 
 Delivery mode In-person at NTI branches and Creativa Innovation Hubs across governorates
 
 Eligibility Egyptian nationals; suitable qualification or final-year student; track-specific prerequisites; admission test
 
 Enrollment rule One training unit/track at a time (to ensure specialization and efficiency)
 
 Attendance requirement Minimum 80% attendance of total program hours 
 
 Certificate One attendance/completion certificate issued per training unit, within ~1 month of completion
 
 
 Enrollment Requirements 
 
 • Must be an Egyptian national. 
 
 • Suitable educational qualification, or be a final-year student.
 • Fulfill the specific prerequisites of the chosen training track.
 • Submit all required enrollment documents.

• Pass the admission test for that track. 
 Required Documents Upon Acceptance 
 
 • Copy of the national ID card. 
 • Copy of the graduation certificate (for graduates). 
 
 • Enrollment certificate or university ID showing current academic year (for students).
 • One personal photo. 
 • Signed commitment statement agreeing to the scholarship conditions (downloaded/uploaded via the
 program website). 
 
 General Rules 
 
 • Create a personal account on the Academy's website to upload documents.
 • Ensure accuracy of all information in the commitment statement.
 • Meet the required attendance (‡ 80% of total hours). 
 • Maintain appropriate conduct with trainers and organizers. 
 
 • Pass required exams to receive attendance/completion certificates.
 • Do not publish course materials online (IP rights). 
 • Submit a new signed commitment statement for each course enrolled in.
 • Withdrawal requests must be sent at least 48 hours before the training start date.
 
 • All official communication goes through ETA@nti.sci.eg. 
 
 Available Training Programs 
 
 The Academy currently lists 6 Huawei-certification-aligned programs. As with the enrollment rules above, a
 trainee can join one track at a time; each unit has its own prerequisites and admission test, and leads
 toward a specific Huawei HCIA-level certification. 
 
 1. Huawei Big Data Associate (HCIA-Big Data) 
 
 Introduces big-data fundamentals and the open-source big-data ecosystem (e.g. Hadoop-family
 components), plus Huawei's big-data platform and solutions. Covers data collection, storage, processing
 and analysis at an associate/foundational level, preparing trainees for the HCIA-Big Data certification
 exam. 
 
 2. Huawei Enterprise Datacom Technologies (HCIA-Datacom) 
 
 A foundational networking track covering data-communication concepts, IP addressing, routing and
 switching, WLAN basics, and network management/maintenance using Huawei enterprise networking
 equipment — the Huawei-certification equivalent of a CCNA-style networking foundation. Prepares
 
 trainees for the HCIA-Datacom exam and is a common prerequisite for more advanced Datacom (HCIP)
 study. 
 
 3. Artificial Intelligence (AI) (HCIA-AI) 
 Covers Python programming fundamentals and the math foundations needed for AI (basic linear algebra,
 probability/statistics), then moves into core AI/ML concepts such as classification, regression, and
 
 clustering, plus Huawei's AI tools and platforms. In its NTI-Aswan run this track was 80 hours across 12
 technical lectures over 2 weeks (morning 9am–3pm or evening 3pm–9pm sessions), open to
 2nd/3rd/4th-year students and graduates of the last 10 years, and leads to the HCIA-AI certification.

4. Cloud Computing (HCIA-Cloud Computing) 
 Introduces core cloud-computing concepts (service/deployment models, virtualization of compute, network
 and storage resources) and Huawei's cloud stack and cloud-service products, building the foundation-level
 
 skills needed for the HCIA-Cloud Computing certification. 
 
 5. HCIA-Security 
 A foundational cybersecurity track covering information-security concepts and basic configuration and
 maintenance of security solutions for small/medium enterprises — firewalls, access control, and core
 security principles — aligned with the HCIA-Security certification. 
 
 6. Master 5G Mobile Network Technology with HCIA-5G 
 
 Covers the evolution of mobile network technologies and 5G network architecture, including 5G radio
 access network and core network fundamentals, terminology, and key technologies — aligned with the
 HCIA-5G certification.
